answer: When handling ornaments in "Una voce poco fa," if there is no grace note, the ornament and the main note are generally sung evenly, dividing the beat. If there is a grace note, it is often sung slightly before the main note. In sections where a grace note appears with a main note that is a quarter note, the main note should be evenly divided into four sixteenth-note sounds. Pay attention to the ornaments in the other two sections of this piece as well.

evidence.text: 꾸밈음에 사선이 없으면 대부분 꾸밈음과 원음이 박자를 나누어 균등하게 노래하고, 사선이 있으면 원음 앞에서 미리 노래하는 경우가 많다. 사선 없는 꾸밈음이 원음인 4분음표와 함께 나오는 부분에서는 원음을 균일하게 나누어 16분음표 네 개의 음형으로 노래한다. 이 곡의 다른 두 꾸밈음 대목에서도 꾸밈음에 유의한다.
evidence.text_en: When a grace note has no slash, the grace note and principal note usually divide the beat and are sung evenly; when it has a slash, it is often sung in advance of the principal note. In a passage where an unslashed grace note appears with a principal quarter note, divide the principal note evenly and sing a figure of four sixteenth notes. Pay attention to the grace notes in the two other ornamented passages in this piece as well.
